Turbulent

/TUR-byuh-lunt/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Turbulent means characterized by conflict, disorder, or sudden violent change; unsettled and disorderly

Turbulent means full of conflict, disorder, or sudden violent change. Below the falls the river turned turbulent, all churning white water and flying spray.

Worked Example

It was a turbulent year for the stock market: prices soared in the spring, crashed in June, and swung wildly all autumn.

The market didn't move smoothly — it lurched through sudden, violent changes with no stability anywhere. Turbulent describes exactly that kind of unsettled, disorderly period, whether in water, weather, politics, or finance.

How Turbulent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

stormy

stormy: full of upheaval, anger, or violent disturbance

tumultuous

tumultuous: loud, disorderly, and confused

unstable

unstable: likely to shift or collapse suddenly

Antonyms

tranquil

tranquil: calm and peaceful

orderly

orderly: well-organized and free of disorder

How Strong Is It? — unsettled → turbulent → explosive

unsettled vs. turbulent

unsettled vs. turbulent: An unsettled situation is uneasy and shifting; a turbulent one is churning with open conflict and disorder.

explosive vs. turbulent

explosive vs. turbulent: Explosive is stronger than turbulent — the disorder is no longer just churning, it is bursting into outright violence.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — turb

Root — turb: uproar, commotion, disorderly crowd (Latin turba)

Suffix — -ulent

Suffix — -ulent: full of (Latin -ulentus)

Put it together

Put it together: Turbulent is literally 'full of commotion' — Latin turba named the noisy chaos of an unruly crowd, and turbulent things still churn like one.

Use the root in a new word: perturb

Use the root in a new word: perturb: The strange reading on the pressure gauge perturbed the engineer, who checked it three times before calling her supervisor.

Root Check

Word Choice

Neutral

Turbulent works literally for air and water (a turbulent river, turbulent skies — on a flight you feel the related noun turbulence) and figuratively for periods, relationships, and emotions: a turbulent decade, a turbulent friendship, turbulent feelings.
